findings.description: A long-term AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables. They are committed to version control, persisted in Terraform state, and readable by any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration.

No kms_key_arn is set, so environment variables holding secrets are protected only by the default AWS-managed key and are returned in cleartext to anyone who can read the function configuration. A customer-managed CMK with a restrictive key policy would provide a separate authorization boundary around these secrets.
The function targets the nodejs12.x runtime, which AWS has deprecated; it no longer receives security patches, so known vulnerabilities in the execution environment remain unfixed.

The function declares no vpc_config, so it executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted egress and no security group or subnet-level segmentation, easing exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the function is abused.

The assume-role trust policy grants sts:AssumeRole to the lambda.amazonaws.com service principal with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, omitting the standard confused-deputy guardrail scoping the trust to functions in this account.
